\subsection{Certificate semantics and correctness}

We first state the theorem-to-JSON implication used by all six links.  For a
finite exact-decimal coefficient tuple \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_d)\), write
\[
 F_c(\lambda)=(1+\lambda)\log(1+\lambda)-\lambda\log\lambda
 +e^{-\lambda}\sum_{j=1}^d c_j\lambda^j.
 \tag{U-C.C.1}\label{up:app-C:eq:c-1}
\]
A file with schema \texttt{corrected-two-sided-ramsey-v1} contains exact
tuples \(c^{\rm prior},c^{\rm target}\), an exact splice
\(\lambda_*\), and a finite ordered list of records
\((\lambda_i^-,\lambda_i^+,M_i,Y_i)\).  Acceptance means that outward-rounded
interval evaluation establishes all of the following obligations.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The records form an exact partition of \([\lambda_*,1]\), with
      \(0<M_i,Y_i<1\), and the prior rate is strictly concave on
      \((0,1]\).
\item On every record and every \(\lambda\) in its closed interval, put
      \[
       X=(1-M_i)
       \bigl(1-e^{-F'_{c^{\rm target}}(\lambda)}\bigr)^{1/(1-M_i)},
       \quad a=-\log X,\quad b=-\log Y_i.
      \]
      The verifier proves \(F_{c^{\rm target}}>0\),
      \(F'_{c^{\rm target}}>0\), and both prior-region inequalities
      \[
       a+\mu b>F_{c^{\rm prior}}(\mu),\qquad
       b+\mu a>F_{c^{\rm prior}}(\mu)
       \quad(0<\mu\le1).                       \tag{U-C.C.2}\label{up:app-C:eq:c-2}
      \]
      Strict concavity reduces the two suprema in \(\mu\) to their endpoint
      and unique stationary-point candidates; every candidate is enclosed.
\item On the same complete record interval the main descent slack satisfies
      \[
       F_{c^{\rm target}}(\lambda)
       +\frac12\{\log X+\lambda\log M_i+\lambda\log Y_i\}>0. \tag{U-C.C.3}\label{up:app-C:eq:c-3}
      \]
\item On the open interval \((0,\lambda_*]\), the verifier takes
      \(M=\lambda e^{-\lambda}\), defines \(X\) by the same formula and
      \(Y=1-X\), and proves positivity of \(F,F'\) and a strictly positive
      lower bound for the left side of \eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-3} divided by \(\lambda\).  Bounds
      \(q_-\lambda\le e^{-F'}\le q_+\lambda\) cancel the two
      \(\lambda\log\lambda\) singularities, so this is an analytic tail
      proof rather than extrapolation from \(\lambda_*\).
\item At the first link, the same elementary witness proves the prior rate.
      At every later link, \(c^{\rm prior}\) agrees entry by entry, as exact
      decimal data, with the preceding accepted target tuple.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{lemma}[Finite-net rate descent]\label{up:lem:finite-net-descent}
Let \(G:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, twice continuously differentiable
on \((0,1]\), and satisfy \(G(0)=0\), \(G,G'>0\).  Suppose
\(G(\lambda)=H(\lambda)+O(\lambda)\) at zero, where
\(H(\lambda)=(1+\lambda)\log(1+\lambda)-\lambda\log\lambda\).
For every \(\lambda\in(0,1]\), suppose there are \(M,X,Y\in(0,1)\) with
\[
 X=(1-M)\bigl(1-e^{-G'(\lambda)}\bigr)^{1/(1-M)}
 \tag{U-C.C.4}\label{up:eq:descent-X}
\]
and
\[
 G(\lambda)+\frac12\{\log X+\lambda\log M+
 \lambda\log Y\}>0.                         \tag{U-C.C.5}\label{up:eq:descent-main}
\]
Assume that on every compact \(I\subset(0,1]\),
\(\inf_I G'>0\), \(\sup_I M<1\), and, for every sufficiently small
\(\delta>0\), the point
\[
 p_{\lambda,\delta}=1-e^{-G'(\lambda)+2\delta},\qquad
 x_{\lambda,\delta}=e^{-\delta}(1-M)
 p_{\lambda,\delta}^{1/(1-M)},              \tag{U-C.C.6}\label{up:app-C:eq:c-6}
\]
paired with \(Y\), lies in \(\mathcal R_*\).  Then, uniformly for
\(1\le\ell\le k\),
\[
 \log R(k,\ell)\le kG(\ell/k)+o(k).          \tag{U-C.C.7}\label{up:app-C:eq:c-7}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(\epsilon>0\).  The Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres recursion and Stirling's
formula give \(\log R(k,\ell)\le kH(\ell/k)+o(k)\), uniformly as
\(\ell/k\to0\).  Since \(H-G=O(\lambda)\), choose \(\rho>0\) so that
the desired bound with error \(\epsilon k\) already holds when
\(\ell\le\rho k\).  It remains to consider \(I=[\rho,1]\).

The hypotheses in the lemma make the logarithm of
\(x_{\lambda,\delta}/X(\lambda)\) converge uniformly to zero as
\(\delta\downarrow0\).  Choose one \(\delta>0\) such that, throughout
\(I\),
\[
 e^{-\epsilon}X(\lambda)\le x_{\lambda,\delta}<X(\lambda).
 \tag{U-C.C.8}\label{up:app-C:eq:c-8}
\]
Uniform continuity of \(G,G'\) supplies a finite descending grid
\(\{\lambda_j\}\) such that every \(r\in I\) has a
\(\lambda_j\in[r,r+h]\) with
\[
 |G(\lambda_j)-G(r)|\le\epsilon/2,qquad
 |G'(\lambda_j)-G'(r)|\le\delta.             \tag{U-C.C.9}\label{up:app-C:eq:c-9}
\]
Apply the balanced-book corollary of Appendix B at each grid point with
\(p=p_{\lambda_j,\delta}\), \(\mu=M(\lambda_j)\),
\(x=x_{\lambda_j,\delta}\), and \(y=Y(\lambda_j)\).  The strict book
hypothesis follows from \eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-6}, and the assumed interior condition supplies
the other hypothesis.  Since the grid is finite, the largest of the
resulting thresholds is finite.

Now let \(N\ge e^{k(G(r)+\epsilon)}\), where \(r=\ell/k\in I\).  If the
red-edge density is at least \(1-e^{-G'(r)+\delta}\), it is at least
\(p_{\lambda_j,\delta}\) by \eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-9}.  Equations
\eqref{up:eq:descent-main}, \eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-8}, \eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-9},
\(\lambda_jk\ge\ell\), and \(\log(MY)<0\) give
\begin{align*}
 N&\ge e^{k(G(\lambda_j)+\epsilon/2)}\\
  &\ge (e^{-\epsilon}X(\lambda_j))^{-k/2}
       (M(\lambda_j)Y(\lambda_j))^{-\ell/2}\\
  &\ge x_{\lambda_j,\delta}^{-k/2}
       (M(\lambda_j)Y(\lambda_j))^{-\ell/2}.
\end{align*}
The balanced-book corollary therefore gives a red \(K_k\) or a blue
\(K_\ell\).

Otherwise the average blue degree is greater than
\(e^{-G'(r)+\delta}(N-1)\), so some vertex has, for all sufficiently large
\(k\), at least
\[
 \exp\{kG(r)+\epsilon k-G'(r)+\delta/2\}       \tag{U-C.C.10}\label{up:app-C:eq:c-10}
\]
blue neighbours.  Induct on \(\ell\), starting with the already settled
range \(\ell\le\rho k\).  For \(r-1/k\ge\rho/2\), the mean-value theorem
gives
\[
 k\{G(r)-G(r-1/k)\}=G'(\xi),\qquad
 G'(r)-G'(\xi)\le k^{-1}
  \sup_{[\rho/2,1]}|G''|\le\delta/2
\]
once \(k\) is large.  Thus \eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-10} is at least the induction threshold
\(e^{k(G((\ell-1)/k)+\epsilon)}\).  Its blue neighbourhood contains a red
\(K_k\), or a blue \(K_{\ell-1}\) which extends with the chosen vertex.
This completes the induction and the uniform \(\epsilon\)-form of \eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-7}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Rate-certificate correctness]\label{up:prop:rate-correctness}
Assume the repaired book induction in Appendix B and Arb's containment
semantics.  If the first certificate satisfies (i)--(v), its target obeys the
uniform Ramsey-rate bound \eqref{up:eq:rate-bound}.  If a finite chain is accepted with the exact
handoffs in (v), every target in the chain obeys that bound; in particular the
sixth target is \(F_6\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On a closed record interval, \eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-2} has strict positive margin in both colour
orientations.  Together with the already proved uniform prior rate, this
allows \(X,Y_i\) to be enlarged slightly while retaining both exponent
bounds; hence \((X,Y_i)\in\mathcal R_*\).  Decreasing the first coordinate to
\(x_{\lambda,\delta}\) preserves interior membership.  The finitely many
records also give \(\sup M_i<1\), and the verifier proves \(F,F'>0\) and
\eqref{up:app-C:eq:c-3}, which are exactly \eqref{up:eq:descent-X}--\eqref{up:eq:descent-main}.

On \((0,\lambda_*]\), the elementary witness has \(Y=1-X\).  Since
\(x_{\lambda,\delta}<X\), choose \(z\) strictly between them.  The elementary
recursion places \((z,1-z)\) in \(\mathcal R\), while
\(x_{\lambda,\delta}<z\) and \(Y<1-z\); therefore the perturbed point lies
in \(\mathcal R_*\).  Obligation (iv) proves the remaining analytic
hypotheses on the whole open interval, including a positive normalized main
slack rather than a sampled extrapolation.  Because every target has the form
\(H(\lambda)+e^{-\lambda}P(\lambda)\) with \(P(0)=0\), its difference from
\(H\) is \(O(\lambda)\).  Thus \cref{up:lem:finite-net-descent} proves one
accepted link.

For the first link the same elementary argument proves the prior.  Exact
entrywise target-to-prior equality then permits ordinary induction through
the six links, without a rounded or refitted intermediate rate.
\end{proof}

\begin{enumerate}
